scenario: Desktop is Screenshot.app's save folder and holds about 1,500 capture-shaped files (Screenshot*.png, Screen Recording*.mov, and any movie file at all), most predating the install. The owner removes 10 recent cards from the Shelf and opens the Shelf daily for a month.

actual_by_code: RecordingPickup.collect inserts every capture-shaped name into `seen` before it tests the date (RecordingPickup.swift:76-85), so files from before the install fill the 1,000 cap. Over the cap, trimSeen keeps names whose file still exists and then takes `Set(kept.prefix(1000))` (:134-140): an arbitrary 1,000 of the 1,500 survive. The ~500 evicted names are re-met on the next open; any with mtime after `since` (:82) is offered again, so a removed card comes back with probability about one third per open. ShelfStore.add (ShelfStore.swift:250-265) builds an icon and a QuickLook thumbnail request for every returned file before the 60-card trim at :263. Because the set is over the cap again at the end of every open, each open (main thread, see F-022) also pays UTType(filenameExtension:) for every file in every capture folder (:96), a resourceValues stat per re-met name (:80), up to folders x 1,500 fileExists calls in trimSeen (:135-139), and a defaults write of 1,000 names (ShelfStore.swift:226) even when nothing changed. scenario: The Now Playing helper dies or goes silent every 10 to 120 seconds (an uncaught Objective-C exception on one player's metadata, G-008; MediaRemote stalling after sleep) for days. It does emit at least one snapshot in each life.
expected: Isla gives up on a helper that keeps dying, falls back to scripting and says so, instead of relaunching it for ever.
actual_by_code: NowPlayingFailurePolicy.recordFailure (:33-52) falls back only on 3 consecutive failures or on the 9th restart within 300 s of the first failure. recordSuccess() runs on every snapshot (NowPlayingFeed.swift:458) and in start() (:151), so consecutive never reaches 3 for a helper that speaks once per life. The delays are 2,4,8,16,32,60,60,60 s (sum 242 s), so nine failures fit inside 300 s only if lives average under about 7 s. At a 10 s life the window expires first (:36-38), the count resets to 1 and the delay returns to 2 s. Result: a helper that lives 10 to 120 s between deaths is relaunched without limit, roughly 800 to 2,000 perl launches a day (arithmetic from the delays above), each a dlopen of MediaRemote, a Log.notice, and a stale island for the 2 to 60 s delay. checkForSilence (:215-232) feeds the same path. The tests cover only sub-second flaps; the 'forgiven after the window' test (testRestartBudgetResetsAfterTheWindow) encodes the elapsed-time forgiveness as intended, but forgiveness is measured from the first failure, not from how long the helper actually survived.

scenario: Spotify account connected; Isla runs for 30 days; the user likes or unlikes tracks in the Spotify app or on a phone after Isla has already looked a track up, then replays them.

scenario: The library index after a year of use: 10,000 folder documents plus a few hundred imports, with a sync client touching the watched folder weekly.
expected: A change to one document rewrites a small amount of data, off the main thread.
actual_by_code: persist() (:614-618) JSON-encodes the whole State (every StoredDocument for every folder file, plus issues, bindings, unassigned imports) and writes it atomically, synchronously, on the main actor. One StoredDocument is about 170 B of JSON (36-char UUID, origin, absolute path; estimate), so 10,000 documents is about 1.7 MB per write. It runs on every rescan that finds any change (:293-296), every bind and unbind (:336-349), every import and every Save Copy (:180), every folder add/remove, and every Clear. Together with the 2x memory peak in the previous row, a single sync event on a large library costs a full parse of every file plus a 1.7 MB encode and write, all on the main thread. Imports are also append-only (see J-025): each Save Copy adds a new UUID.lrc, a new record and a new index row, and every one is re-read at every launch (reloadImportedRecords, :489-499).

actual_by_code: Each snapshot that carries artwork starts its own decode on `DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated)` (MediaController.swift:1582-1587, 1672-1697). Nothing cancels a decode whose track has already moved on: the staleness check (`artworkKey == key`) runs only after the decode, on the main queue (:1693-1696). scenario: Clipboard poll over 30 days of uptime, including another app that rewrites the pasteboard continuously (a clipboard manager re-asserting contents, a remote-desktop or VM bridge).
expected: The poll stays cheap; a chatty writer cannot make Isla read large clipboard data many times a second.

Cost scales with the number of changes, not time: every change costs availableType, a data(forType:) probe for the internal marker, and readObjects(NSURL) (:178-185); with screenshots on it also walks all pasteboard types for movie conformance and reads a movie whole into memory (:198-209, 231-239); then pasteboard.string(forType:) reads the entire string before the 256 KiB cap is applied (:215-217, 258-261). A writer changing the pasteboard at 2 Hz therefore makes Isla do those reads at 2 Hz, each up to the full size of whatever is on the pasteboard, on the main thread; there is no rate limit or backoff. Memory after the cap is bounded at 40 x 256 KiB. Overlaps J-001 (privacy read behaviour) and the round-2 read-stall row; the rate dimension is new.

On failure write() falls to the file (:90-91) while the delete at :134 may or may not have run. The cache is written through (:570) so the session works regardless.

No Settings text for tokenUnavailable exists (SettingsPane.swift:470-493).

If one item lands in the file and an older one for the same account survives in the keychain (delete at :134 failed), the stale keychain value wins. Disconnect clears both (:94-99). Effect is a connected-looking dead account after a keychain reset.

actual_by_code: current() decides presence only from AudioObjectHasProperty plus a successful read (SystemVolume.swift:50-63), ignoring IsPropertySettable. The bar therefore draws. set() returns false when not settable (:73-76) but both callers drop the result (LockScreenCard.swift:719, :743). The bar follows the finger during the drag, and onEnded then snaps it back to the device's real level (:722), which is exactly the dead slider the file comment disclaims.

scenario: Multi-channel interface (4-18 outputs) whose volume lives on channels 3+ or on all channels with no main control
expected: Bar reflects and sets the device's real level, or is hidden.
actual_by_code: current() reads main, then channels 1 and 2 only (SystemVolume.swift:19-31). set() writes main, else channels 1 and 2 only (:40-45). dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Device briefly drops out of available() during a stream reconfiguration (sample-rate change, Bluetooth A2DP to HFP switch when a call starts) and a refresh is triggered inside that window
expected: The device reappears once the reconfiguration ends.
actual_by_code: hasOutputStreams requires mNumberChannels > 0 (AudioOutputs.swift:176-180), so a device mid-reconfiguration (zero channels or a size-0 answer) is dropped from the read. No listener covers sample-rate or stream-configuration changes, and none covers the device list (see the hot-plug rows), so a refresh caused by a volume or default event during that window publishes a list missing the device. Nothing corrects it until the next event or pane change. Sample-rate changes by themselves change nothing the card shows.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: coreaudiod restarts (Bluetooth stack reset, USB audio crash, wake) with the lock card up
expected: Card re-resolves devices; selection still works.
actual_by_code: No kAudioHardwarePropertyServiceRestarted listener and no kAudioHardwarePropertyRunLoop setup (grep: none). After a restart all AudioDeviceIDs may be renumbered. currentOutput, Output.id and listeningTo hold old IDs, so select(oldID) fails silently, and the per-device volume listener sits on a dead ID. A re-read happens only if the system-object default listener survives the restart and fires. Apple's documented pattern is to watch ServiceRestarted and rebuild. Behaviour after a real restart cannot be traced from code.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Listener lifecycle over hundreds of lock/unlock cycles
expected: Every add has a matching remove; nothing accumulates.
actual_by_code: present() creates one AudioWatch and start() installs the system listener once plus one volume listener (LockCardWindow.swift:94-96; AudioOutputs.swift:335-344, :382-407). dismiss() calls stop(), which removes both (LockCardWindow.swift:166-173; AudioOutputs.swift:346-351, :409-425). A second present() while up only re-reads (:75-86). deinit is a safety net (:353-359). Balanced. Cost is the per-lock churn from F-026 (listeners and enumeration when nothing plays), not a leak.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: The volume listener is replaced from inside its own callback (the default and the old device's volume change in the same event burst)
expected: Removing the currently running block is safe.
actual_by_code: refresh runs inside the volume block, finds a new default, and installCoreAudioListeners removes volumeListener, the very block that is executing, then adds a new one (AudioOutputs.swift:405-406, :435-451). The code comment (:376-381) proves safety only for the system listener. Removing a block on its own queue from within its callback is normally allowed, but the comment's reasoning does not cover this path.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: AudioOutputs.available() cost on the main actor: lock present(), every pane change, every default or volume event, and AmbientWatch.devicesChanged on every device-list notification
expected: Bounded and cheap; never blocks the lock transition.
actual_by_code: Per device: StreamConfiguration size+data, Name, TransportType, DataSource has+get, about 6 synchronous HAL calls, plus 3 for the volume (AudioOutputs.swift:29-50, :168-213). It runs synchronously in AudioWatch.start() inside present() (LockCardWindow.swift:94-95) and in AmbientWatch.devicesChanged for each notification (AmbientWatch.swift:136-141, :181-188), which are bursty and not coalesced. Apps that churn aggregate or virtual devices (Zoom, Loopback, Chrome capture) re-run the enumeration on main each time. A device stalled mid-connect (Bluetooth, AirPlay) can block the main actor inside lock present. No timing exists. F-045 covers only the volume-drag multiplication.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Two outputs share a name (two identical USB DACs, two 'AirPods' of different owners) or the default device has an empty name
expected: Distinguishable rows; the current device is always listed and highlighted.
actual_by_code: Rows show only name and glyph (LockScreenCard.swift:577-584), so identical names are indistinguishable except by highlight. dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: HomePod, Apple TV or AirPlay 2 speakers that Control Center lists but are not CoreAudio devices until connected
expected: The card's Sound Output reaches them, as the reference cards do.
actual_by_code: The picker is built only from kAudioHardwarePropertyDevices (AudioOutputs.swift:29-50). Unconnected AirPlay endpoints are not HAL devices, so they are not offered and cannot be started from the card. The generic 'airplayaudio' glyph is just the no-current-device fallback (LockScreenCard.swift:829). The doc comment (AudioOutputs.swift:5-12) frames this as switching the system default, so it is a capability gap rather than a bug.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Volume read back immediately after a write on a Bluetooth output (VoiceOver adjust or drag release)
expected: Bar shows the new level and stays there.
actual_by_code: Adjust: SystemVolume.set(next); volume = SystemVolume.current() ?? next (LockScreenCard.swift:743-744). Release: volume = SystemVolume.current() ?? draggingVolume (:722). A Bluetooth or USB device whose scalar read lags the write (absolute-volume handshake) returns the OLD level, so the bar snaps back and then jumps forward when the volume listener finally fires (:187-189). Whether macOS devices lag is unknown from code.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Artwork over 4 MB (a local FLAC/ALAC library with 5-10 MB embedded PNG covers played in a non-Music player)
expected: A cover appears, or a downscaled one; if not possible, a placeholder after the normal wait.
actual_by_code: The helper attaches the artwork and sets sArtworkID as delivered (helper.m:293-298). The decoder drops anything over 4 MB without trace (NowPlayingPayloadDecoder.swift:34-38, :54) while the rest of the snapshot is kept. The app then asks once (MediaController.swift:1588-1595, helper.m:379-396), the helper sends the same oversized bytes, and they are dropped again. artworkRequestedFor now holds the key, so the cover is gone for the track (placeholder after 2.5 s, MediaPane.swift:238-250). No downscale exists in the helper. No decoder test covers the cap.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: A 1-4 MB cover arrives (large Spotify/Apple Music hi-res, local file art) on the helper route
expected: Track change stays smooth; the comment on decodeArtwork says heavy work is off-main.
actual_by_code: Only the image decode is off-main (MediaController.swift:1672-1698). The pipe chunk goes Task{@MainActor} to consume (NowPlayingFeed.swift:291, :442). NDJSONBuffer.append runs on main and rescans the whole pending buffer with firstIndex(of: 0x0A) after every chunk (NDJSONBuffer.swift:31-36), which is quadratic in record size over 16-64 KB pipe reads. Then JSONSerialization, base64.count (O(n) grapheme count) and Data(base64Encoded:) also run on main (NowPlayingPayloadDecoder.swift:34-37). A 5.6 MB line is plausibly hundreds of ms of main-thread time; unmeasured. Typical 100-300 KB covers are fine.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Rapid skipping through 10+ tracks with 2000-3000 px covers (Spotify Next held down)
expected: Stale decodes are cancelled or bounded.
actual_by_code: Each snapshot with artwork starts DispatchQueue.global(qos:.userInitiated).async decodes with no cap or cancellation (MediaController.swift:1677). The key guard discards stale results afterwards (:1684, :1694) but not the work. Each decode holds about 36 MB (F-044) plus the base64 and Data copies, so a burst can hold hundreds of MB transiently and compete with the foreground. The helper resends a cover per song because the title is in the artwork id (helper.m:293-294).

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Two different cover payloads for the same track key decode concurrently (low-res placeholder then hi-res, or an 'art' re-request answered alongside a normal publish)
expected: The newest payload wins.
actual_by_code: decodeArtwork guards only artworkKey == key at completion (MediaController.swift:1684, :1694), and decodes run on a concurrent global queue. There is no sequence number, so a slower older decode can finish last and overwrite the newer image. Identical payloads are harmless. Different ones need a player that re-publishes a better cover without changing title or artwork id (artwork id changes do re-send, helper.m:296).

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Fallback route (helper refused or Gatekeeper-blocked, the DMG case) with a skip to the next song
expected: Same polish as the helper route: old cover held about 180 ms, album-mates keep the cover (filmed fix of 2026-09-21).
actual_by_code: refreshFromPlayers sets artwork = nil at once when state.key changes (MediaController.swift:1853-1855) and then waits for a Spotify CDN fetch or a Music AppleScript transfer (:1856-1859). It has no 180 ms grace (:1622-1627) and no album-mate reuse (:1596-1607). Every skip flashes cover to skeleton to cover (up to the 2.5 s placeholder if slow). The lock card also loses its coverLight at that moment, so on macOS 26 the glass flips type (see the glass-swap row).

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Fallback or held route cover fetch fails once (offline blip, Spotify CDN timeout, Music script returns nothing) while the track plays on
expected: A retry once per track, as the helper route has (shouldAskForArtwork), or a quiet placeholder.
actual_by_code: artworkKey is set before the fetch (MediaController.swift:1854); on failure the callback assigns nil and the next refreshFromPlayers returns early because artworkKey == state.key (:1853). shouldAskForArtwork requires feedAvailable (:1653), which is false on the fallback, so the once-per-track recovery cannot run. The held route behaves the same: fetchHeldArtwork on a nil image does nothing and is called again only when the title changes (:1299-1308, :1358). The URLSession.shared request uses the 60 s default timeout and no retry (PlayerBridge.swift:240).

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)

expected: No fetch, no crash, placeholder after the wait.
actual_by_code: URL(string:) failure gives artworkURL nil (PlayerBridge.swift:411); a scheme other than https returns completion(nil) (:237-239) with no network call. The cover then waits out the 2.5 s skeleton and shows the note placeholder. Silent but safe.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Spotify returns 'missing value' for artwork url (local files, ads, some podcast episodes) on the AppleScript fallback
expected: Title, position and play state still read; only the cover is absent.
actual_by_code: The state script concatenates (artwork url of currentTrackRef) at the end of one expression (PlayerBridge.swift:284). If that property is missing value, AppleScript raises a coercion error inside the try block, the script returns 'error' plus the number, and interpret() maps any code other than -1728/-600 to .unknown (:395-400). The whole state answer is lost, not just the cover. Whether Spotify ever returns missing value there cannot be told without the app; PlayerScriptTests only compile the script.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)

NSImage(data:) defers pixel decoding to the first draw, which happens on the main thread in the open panel or lock card. The helper route forces the decode via NSBitmapImageRep.cgImage on a global queue (MediaController.swift:1678). The CDN fetch has no size cap or status check either (:240-243). Draw-time hitch size not measured.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Browser tab or app supplies a degenerate cover: 16x16 favicon, 1x1 pixel, solid white, letterboxed 4:3 YouTube thumbnail
expected: Treated as no usable cover (placeholder) or at least not blown up into the 118 pt and lock-card light.
actual_by_code: Any decodable image becomes artwork (MediaController.swift:1689-1695); there is no minimum-size or flatness check. A 16x16 icon is scaled to 118 pt and blown up to a 1.5x blurred wash in the lock card (LockScreenCard.swift:209-219). It also suppresses the placeholder and the ask-again path (showing == true, :1651). A flat white image is the worst case for F-003. A 4:3 letterboxed thumbnail is aspect-filled so the black bars show in the square crop.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Undecodable cover (SVG, PDF, truncated JPEG, unsupported format) arrives for the displayed track
expected: No stale previous cover; placeholder after the wait; no crash.
actual_by_code: NSBitmapImageRep(data:) fails, and the main hop sets artwork = nil if artworkKey is still this key (MediaController.swift:1678-1687). Since artwork data existed the earlier blank was cancelled (:1583-1584), so this nil assignment is what clears the old cover. artworkRequestedFor already has the key (:1586), so there is no re-ask and the cover stays absent for the track. Safe and silent. Animated GIF/APNG decode to frame 0.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: CMYK JPEG, 16-bit PNG, grayscale or Display P3 wide-gamut cover through the lock-card cover light and the lyrics stage ambience
expected: Plausible colours with no banding or colour-space crash.
actual_by_code: rep.cgImage keeps the source colour space (MediaController.swift:1678-1692) and Image(nsImage:) draws it. The cover light applies .saturation(1.3) and .blur(44, opaque: true) (LockScreenCard.swift:211-219), the stage .blur(60) with opacity 0.35 (LyricsStage.swift:180-189). How SwiftUI's offscreen blur path handles a CMYK CGImage source, or whether wide-gamut covers glow oversaturated against the sRGB card, cannot be traced from code. No fixtures exist.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Cover with an alpha channel (transparent PNG logo, podcast art on transparency) under the lock-card cover light
expected: Light derived from the visible art; transparent areas not read as black.
actual_by_code: coverLight draws the image with .blur(radius: 44, opaque: true) (LockScreenCard.swift:218). opaque: true treats transparent pixels as opaque, so transparent regions blur to black or dark fringe and the 0.34 black wash sits on top (:220). The result is a much darker, muddier card than the cover implies. The 76 pt thumbnail (:269) lets the card glass show through the same transparent regions.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Macs on macOS 26+: track change (or a cover that fails to decode) while the lock-card scrubber or volume bar is being dragged
expected: The drag ends cleanly; seek/volume state never gets stuck.
actual_by_code: LockScreenCard passes samplesBackdrop: style != .solid && media.artwork == nil (LockScreenCard.swift:155). GlassSurfaceStyle.usesSystemGlass depends on it (GlassSurface.swift:242) and its body branches between content.glassEffect and the drawn recipe (:253-254, :294-300). A cover that goes nil (fallback-route skip, or the 180 ms blank at MediaController.swift:1622-1627) changes the branch, so the whole card content subtree is re-created and an in-flight DragGesture is torn down without onEnded. scrubbing and draggingVolume are @State on LockScreenCard (:60, :67), which survive. scrubbing stays set, so the bar pins to the old finger fraction (:620-621), and a stuck draggingVolume blocks the volume mirror (:188) until the next drag. Every coverless track and every fallback-route skip also flashes real glass versus drawn glass.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Opening the panel right after a skip, with a fresh multi-megapixel cover that has only been drawn at 22 pt (or not at all) in the compact pill
expected: The 22 to 118 pt morph runs at full frame rate.
actual_by_code: The same NSImage object (full pixel size, MediaController.swift:1689-1692) is drawn by compactArtwork (NotchContentView.swift:696-700) and by MediaPane.artwork (MediaPane.swift:227-232) under one matched-geometry id (:272, NotchContentView.swift:735). Nothing pre-scales it, so the first 118 pt draw within the 0.34 s spring may include a texture upload and downsample of the full bitmap. Not measured; this is the F-044 cost surfacing at the morph.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Music.app plays a streaming (non-library) track on the AppleScript fallback and cover is requested
expected: Cover shown, or a quick placeholder.
actual_by_code: The script returns missing value when count of artworks of current track is 0 (PlayerBridge.swift:351-356), then completion(nil) (:246). For cloud or radio tracks the artworks list may be empty, in which case there is never a cover on the fallback route. Not traceable without the app. A large raw artwork transfer also runs at .background priority on the one serial AppleScript queue (:471-501), so a Next tap issued just after a skip can wait behind the transfer. F-025 notes no timeout but not this cover transfer.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: Helper receives an artwork value that is not NSData (NSNull or NSString from a misbehaving player's Now Playing info)
expected: Ignored; helper stays up.
actual_by_code: helper.m:295-298 reads `NSData *artwork = info[...ArtworkData]` and calls artwork.length and base64EncodedStringWithOptions: with no isKindOfClass check, unlike mediaType and isMusicApp which are checked (:270-272, :275). The file has no @try/@catch. An NSString would pass length > 0 and then throw unrecognized selector, killing the helper. Three quick deaths push the app to the fallback (the failure pattern in round-1 finding G-0xx for +inf duration). Whether any player sends a non-NSData is unknown.

dimension: Audio output hot-plug (lock-card picker, AudioWatch, SystemVolume, AmbientWatch) and the artwork pipeline (helper, fallback, held route, decode, cover light, morph)
scenario: COVERAGE NOTE
expected: n/a
actual_by_code: Already covered, not repeated: F-032 (five-device cap), F-045 (volume-drag enumeration), G-023 (absolute set, balance, mute), F-044 (full-resolution decode, large blurs), F-003 (pale cover contrast), F-026 (per-lock watch), G-030 (CDN fetch privacy claim), the wake-retry cover blink, the oversize-record resync, and the mute row in the ledger. The audio area is thin on live-event handling: the code has only two listener kinds (default device, volume scalar on the default device), and nothing for the device list, data source, alive, mute, service restart or stream configuration. About half of this round is therefore 'unhandled' or 'unknown' and needs hardware (AirPods, a USB DAC with fixed volume, BlackHole, a multi-channel interface) or Instruments. The artwork area is well covered on the helper route (ArtworkRecoveryTests, album-mate reuse, 180 ms grace) and weak on the fallback and held routes, on pathological images (dimension bomb, over 4 MB, degenerate sizes) and on the glass-swap interaction. Not enumerated: HDR or gain-map covers, Image(nsImage:) cache behaviour, and per-display scale-factor changes (unknown without Instruments).
